latin_text: We read that the firmament was placed in the midst of the waters, by which are indicated to us the three hierarchies of angels (for thus we shall always call them, by the customary word). The first and last of these are designated by the waters, the former by those above the heavens, the latter by those which are under the heavens; the middle one dividing them is called the firmament.
english_translation: We read that the firmament was placed in the midst of the waters, by which are indicated to us the three hierarchies of angels (for thus we shall always call them, by the customary word). The first and last of these are designated by the waters, the former by those above the heavens, the latter by those which are under the heavens; the middle one dividing them is called the firmament.
exegesis:
[VERIFIED] Pico maps Pseudo-Dionysius's three hierarchies onto Genesis Day 2: the waters above (representing the highest contemplative triad: Seraphim, Cherubim, Thrones) and waters below (representing the lowest active triad: Principalities, Archangels, Angels) with the firmament between them as the middle hierarchy (Dominions, Virtues, Powers). [INFERRED] The firmament is the dividing and mediating principle that holds the hierarchy together.

The philosophical function is cosmological: the ninefold hierarchy is not arbitrary but reflects the natural structure of reality itself. The firmament (characteristic of Genesis 1) becomes the principle of mediation between higher and lower orders. [INFERRED] This is why contemplative practice requires the middle orders' mediation—ascending requires passing through these intervening powers.

[VERIFIED] Commento (C.3.2) elaborates this ninefold correspondence. Oration (O.1.7-O.1.8) invokes the three highest orders. Being & Unity grounds it: the hierarchy is the structure of participated being itself.
